page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on KVM virtualization and powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Networking is provisioned with a 7 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent data to be backed by remote block storage volumes.

Benchmark results place the ecs.g7a.4xlarge consistently within the median tier for both compute and application-level workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1536.0 and a multi-core score of 8861.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21235.7. Cache throughput remains stable, with small-block read bandwidth reaching 1033.55 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached memory operations register in the lower quartile, recording 39.33 GB/sec for reads and 18.82 GB/sec for writes. In small language model inference, text generation using a 135M parameter model reaches a strong 307.15 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides predictable dedicated compute resources with standard memory density for general enterprise tasks. The primary trade-off lies in the reduced uncached memory throughput and the reliance on external network storage for disk I/O. The ecs.g7a.4xlarge is appropriate for medium-traffic web serving, microservices architectures, application backends, and balanced general-purpose caching environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at 2.55 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 resource allocation. The instance features a 7 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without integrated GPUs, and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence. In standard benchmarks, the instance yields median performance across integer compute, compression, and application tasks, highlighted by 15.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.72 GB/sec web serving throughput. A performance tradeoff appears in uncached memory bandwidth, which ranks in the lower quartile. The instance is suited for general enterprise workloads, web application hosting, caching nodes, and microservices.
